problems.title: Recognize two nested squares
problems.question: Simplify $\sqrt{6-\sqrt{17-12\sqrt2}}$.
problems.idea: Find a square of the form (u−v√2)².
steps: The inner square root is 3−2√2.
The outer radicand is 3+2√2=(1+√2)².

problems.title: A maximum proved by a square
problems.question: Find the maximum of x/(4x²+3x+1) for real x.
problems.idea: Compare it directly with 1/7.
steps: Since the denominator is positive, (2x−1)²≥0 implies 7x≤4x²+3x+1.
Divide to get x/(4x²+3x+1)≤1/7.
Equality holds at x=1/2.

problems.title: An increasing linear function
problems.question: Find the greatest integer n such that y=(8−3n)x−7 is increasing.
problems.idea: A linear function increases exactly when its slope is positive.
steps: This gives n<8/3, so the greatest integer is 2.

problems.title: Add the maximum and minimum on a closed interval
problems.question: Find the sum of the maximum and minimum of y=x²−4x−6 on [−2,3].
problems.idea: Check the vertex and both endpoints.
steps: The minimum is −10 at x=2.
The endpoint values are y(−2)=6 and y(3)=−9, so the maximum is 6.
Their sum is −4.

problems.title: Reflect an input across a parabola’s axis
problems.question: f(x)=−x²+bx+c and f(−3)=f(7). Solve f(x)=f(11).
problems.idea: Equal-height inputs of a parabola are symmetric about its axis.
formulas: Axis x=(−3+7)/2=2; paired inputs sum to 4.
steps: The input paired with 11 is 4−11=−7.
Thus both x=11 and x=−7 solve the equation.
problems.answer: x=−7 or x=11; the listed nontrivial solution is −7.
problems.note: The equation has two solutions. The multiple-choice list includes only −7.

problems.title: A quadratic nonnegative for every input
problems.question: y=x²+px+q is nonnegative for all real x. Find the minimum possible p+q.
problems.idea: The completed square gives the restriction on q.
steps: Then p+q≥p+p²/4=(p+2)²/4−1.
The lower bound −1 is attained with p=−2,q=1, giving y=(x−1)².

problems.title: Two specified cards next to each other
problems.question: Cards 1,2,3,4 are randomly arranged in a row. Find the probability that the odd-numbered cards are adjacent.
problems.idea: Treat cards 1 and 3 as one block.
steps: There are two orders within the block and 3! orders of the block and the remaining cards.
The probability is 12/24.

problems.title: A floor-square-root recurrence
problems.question: a₁=4 and aₙ₊₁=⌊√aₙ⌋. Find a₂₀₁₈.
problems.idea: Compute until the sequence reaches a fixed point.
steps: Thus the sequence begins 4,2,1,1,… and remains 1 from the third term onward.

problems.title: A reciprocal radical identity in an arithmetic progression
problems.question: Positive a,b,c are consecutive arithmetic-progression terms. Simplify $1/(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)+1/(\sqrt b+\sqrt c)$.
problems.idea: Rationalize both denominators using their common squared difference.
steps: For d≠0 the sum is (√b−√a)/d+(√c−√b)/d=(√c−√a)/d.
Since c−a=2d, this equals 2/(√a+√c).
If d=0, a=b=c, and both the original sum and the same formula equal 1/√a.

problems.title: Solve for the number of progression terms
problems.question: Find positive integer n if 7+13+19+⋯+(6n+1)=480.
problems.idea: Use the arithmetic-series sum formula.
steps: Only n=12 is positive.

problems.title: A geometric product from a sum and reciprocal sum
problems.question: A nonzero geometric progression satisfies Σbᵢ=A and Σ1/bᵢ=B for its first 100 terms. Find their product.
problems.idea: Each pair of terms equally far from the ends has the same product T.
steps: If A and B are nonzero, T=A/B and the required product is (A/B)⁵⁰.
If A=B=0, this reasoning cannot divide by B. For example, ratio −1 gives zero for both sums for any nonzero first term, while the product varies.
Therefore no fixed numerical answer follows from the printed information.
problems.answer: (A/B)⁵⁰ when B≠0; not determined by A=B=0.
problems.note: The numerical choices 0,1,2,3,4,5 do not describe the general answer. The zero-sum case needs additional information.

problems.title: A geometric series with a radical ratio
problems.question: Simplify $\sqrt x+\sqrt x/(1+\sqrt x)+\sqrt x/(1+\sqrt x)^2+\cdots$.
problems.idea: For x>0, use the infinite geometric-series formula.
steps: For x>0 the ratio lies between 0 and 1.
At x=0 every term in the original series is zero, so its sum is 0. Negative x is outside the real domain.
problems.note: The usual printed answer 1+√x requires x>0. It does not give the value of the original series at x=0.

problems.title: An inequality valid for every parameter in an interval
problems.question: Find all x such that $(b+x+7)/(2b-x)\ge1/2$ for every $b\in[1,2]$.
problems.idea: Combine the fractions and prevent any denominator zero in the whole interval.
steps: If 2≤x≤4, the denominator vanishes at b=x/2, so those x fail.
If x<2, every denominator is positive, so 3x+14≥0 gives x≥−14/3.
If x>4, every denominator is negative but 3x+14>0, so the inequality fails.

problems.title: The shaded portions of two overlapping rectangles
problems.question: A square has side 8. An overlapping rectangle has sides 2 and 14 as shown. Find the sum of the shaded areas.
problems.idea: The overlap is unshaded and has dimensions 8 by 2.
steps: The areas are 64,28 and 16 respectively.
The shaded total is 64+28−32=60.

problems.title: Convert an arc length to degrees
problems.question: A circle of radius 25 cm has an arc of length π cm. Find the angle subtended by the arc in degrees.
problems.idea: First calculate the angle in radians.
formulas: s=rθ; radians to degrees: multiply by 180°/π.
steps: θ=π/25 radians.
In degrees, θ=180°/25=7.2°.

problems.title: Equal triangle areas and a missing condition
problems.question: O is inside quadrilateral ABCD, and triangles AOC,BOC,AOB have equal areas. Find the length of DA+DC+DB if DO=(12,−5).
problems.idea: If O is inside triangle ABC, the equal areas make O its centroid; check what the wording actually guarantees.
steps: Under the intended centroid interpretation, the vector sum has length 3·13=39.
But the statement only places O inside the quadrilateral, which need not put it inside triangle ABC. Equal unsigned areas alone can also describe exterior points of ABC.
Thus the literal conditions do not force the centroid relation; in either interpretation the listed numerical choices do not justify 13.
problems.answer: 39 under the additional condition O lies inside triangle ABC; otherwise not uniquely determined.
problems.note: The question omits the needed placement condition. Even with that condition, the answer is 39, absent from the choices.

problems.title: A trapezoid with perpendicular diagonals
problems.question: A trapezoid has perpendicular diagonals, one of length 12 cm, and midline 10 cm. Find its area.
problems.idea: For perpendicular diagonals their squared lengths sum to the square of the base sum.
steps: The area is 12·16/2=96.

problems.title: Equidistant from both axes and a fixed point
problems.question: Which listed point is equally distant from both coordinate axes and A=(3,6)?
problems.idea: Equal distances to the axes require |x|=|y|.
formulas: For (t,t), distance to either axis=|t|; squared distance to A=(t−3)²+(t−6)².
steps: Equating gives t²−18t+45=0, with t=3 or 15.
Thus (3,3) and (15,15) both satisfy the conditions; only (15,15) is listed.
For points (t,−t), the equation t²+6t+45=0 has no real roots.
problems.answer: The listed point (15,15); also (3,3) satisfies the conditions.
problems.note: The question asks which listed point works; it does not mean that the geometric point is unique.

problems.title: The central hexagon in a six-pointed star
problems.question: A regular hexagon ABCDEF has side 12 cm. Find the shaded central hexagon formed by triangles ACE and BDF.
problems.idea: The two large equilateral triangles form a regular central hexagon.
formulas: Its side is s/√3; regular hexagon area=3√3·side²/2.
steps: For example, putting the outer hexagon’s leftmost vertex at (−s,0), the central left vertical edge has endpoints (−s/2,±s/(2√3)), so its length is s/√3.
With s=12 the central side is 4√3.

problems.title: Find the foot of a perpendicular on a square’s side
problems.question: M,N,P,K are consecutive square vertices. P=(3,9) and side MK lies on y=0.5x+2. Find the sum of K’s coordinates.
problems.idea: PK is perpendicular to the adjacent side MK.
steps: Intersect with y=x/2+2: (5/2)x=13, giving x=26/5.
Then y=23/5. Their sum is 49/5=9.8.
problems.note: No printed choice equals 9.8. MK is a side because the vertices are given in consecutive order.

problems.title: The largest of five distinct natural numbers
problems.question: Five distinct positive integers have mean 5. How large can the largest be?
problems.idea: Minimize the sum of the other four.
steps: The smallest four distinct positive integers are 1,2,3,4, whose sum is 10.
The largest can therefore be at most 25−10=15.
The set {1,2,3,4,15} attains this bound.

problems.title: Angle between two section lines in a rectangle
problems.question: In rectangle ABCD, AB=10,BC=12. BM:MN:NC=3:2:1, AP:BP=2:3 and AK:KD=1:5. Find the cosine of the acute angle between PN and KM.
problems.idea: Place the rectangle on coordinate axes.
steps: The division points are M=(10,6),N=(10,10),P=(4,0),K=(0,2).
PN=(6,10), KM=(10,4). Their dot product is 100.
Their lengths are 2√34 and 2√29. Divide to get 25/(√29√34).

problems.title: Coordinates on a parabola determine a dot product
problems.question: A=(1,a) and B=(b,1) lie on y=x²−4x+5. Find OA·OB.
problems.idea: Evaluate the function at x=1 and solve for the input giving y=1.
steps: a=2 and (b−2)²=0 gives b=2.
Thus OA=(1,2), OB=(2,1), and their dot product is 1·2+2·1.

problems.title: A tangent chord and an inner sector
problems.question: Two circles are concentric. A chord AB of the larger circle is tangent to the smaller one and divides the larger circumference in ratio 1:2. AB=18. Find the shaded inner sector shown.
problems.idea: The minor central angle is 120°. Use its half-angle to find both radii.
formulas: AB=2R sin60°; inner radius r=R cos60°; sector area=(θ/360°)πr².
steps: The inner shaded sector has angle 120° and radius squared 27.
Its area is (1/3)π·27.

problems.title: Three consecutive integers are divisible by six
problems.question: For a positive integer n, find the remainder of n³−n on division by 6.
problems.idea: Factor into three consecutive integers.
steps: Among three consecutive integers at least one is even and at least one is divisible by 3.
Their product is therefore divisible by both 2 and 3, hence by 6.
